title: Practice: angle geometry problems
intro: Ten questions. Several use the parallel-lines diagram: click the angle asked for.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $a$. Click the angle that is **corresponding** to $a$.
hints: Corresponding angles are in the same position at each crossing — an F shape.
questions.explanation: $a$ is above the top line, right of the crossing line. The corresponding angle is in the same position at the bottom crossing.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $a$. Click the angle that is **alternate** to $a$.
hints: Alternate angles sit inside the parallel lines on opposite sides of the crossing line — a Z shape.
questions.explanation: $a$ is between the lines on the left of the crossing line, so its alternate angle is between the lines on the **right**, at the other crossing.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $b$. Click the angle that is **co-interior** to $b$ (the two add to $180^\circ$).
hints: Co-interior angles are both between the lines, on the **same** side of the crossing line — a C shape.
questions.explanation: $b$ is between the lines on the right, so its co-interior partner is also between the lines on the right, at the bottom crossing.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $c$. Click the angle **vertically opposite** $c$.
hints: Vertically opposite angles share a corner and face each other across it.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are at the same crossing, directly across from each other.

questions.prompt: Match each angle pair to its rule.
hints: Two of these pairs are equal and two add to 180°.
questions.explanation: Z → equal, F → equal, C → supplementary. Angles on a straight line are also supplementary.

questions.scenario: ABCD is a trapezium with AD ∥ BC. AB = AD, and angle DBC $= 41^\circ$.

steps.prompt: Angle ABD (base angles of the isosceles triangle ABD are equal):

questions.explanation: Alternate angles give $41^\circ$; the isosceles triangle gives another $41^\circ$; $180 - 82 = 98^\circ$, not $90^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One of the co-interior angles is $103^\circ$. What is the other?
A parallelogram has neighbouring angles $2y$ and $8y$. What is the size of the **larger** angle?
questions.explanation: $10y = 180 \Rightarrow y = 18$, so the angles are $36^\circ$ and $144^\circ$.

questions.prompt: A line crosses two parallel lines. At one crossing the angles on one side are $3a$ and $2a$, and they lie on a straight line. Find $a$.
In a triangle drawn between two parallel lines, the two base angles are alternate to angles of $67^\circ$ and $54^\circ$ on the top line. What is the third angle of the triangle?
